title: What does the coefficient mean
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 17 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **17 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 6 Easy, 8 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're given a context equation ax + by = c and asked how much more (or what) one unit of one item is worth than another, or what a number in the equation represents.
- The answer is a small number built from the coefficients, not a solution for x or y.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Each coefficient is the value of one unit of the item its variable counts.
- 2) For a 'how many more' question, subtract the two coefficients in the order asked.
- 3) The constant on the other side is the total, not a per-item amount.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Nothing needs solving; you only have to read what each coefficient means.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You try to solve for x or y, or you answer with a single coefficient, the sum of the coefficients, or the total.
Watch the direction of the subtraction when the question says one item is worth more than the other.
